1	# Complete the edge-graph scientific capability
2	
3	The source tree is a real intermediate snapshot from the development of an
4	atomistic-model backend. It contains the first public data contract for a
5	`NeighborGraph`, but the surrounding scientific capability is incomplete.
6	
7	A downstream model must be able to start from atom coordinates and, for both
8	ordinary and periodic systems, construct a graph whose edges represent the
9	neighbor displacements used by the potential-energy model. The same graph must
10	remain usable when the number of edges is padded for a compiled/static backend.
11	Per-edge energy derivatives must then be transformed into per-atom forces,
12	per-atom virials, and one virial for each frame. Empty frames, isolated atoms,
13	virtual atoms, periodic-image neighbors, and padded guard edges are all valid
14	scientific situations rather than exceptional test-only cases.
15	
16	Inspect the source context, run `python reproduce.py`, and
17	complete the reusable capability under `source/`. Preserve the public data
18	contract where it is already meaningful, and keep the implementation usable
19	with NumPy and the array-API style used by the source snapshot.
20	
21	The package-level public API for the completed capability is explicit. Export
22	these names from `deepmd.dpmodel.utils` (the implementation may live in any
23	module under `deepmd/dpmodel/utils/`):
24	
25	- `build_neighbor_graph`
26	- `from_dense_quartet`
27	- `node_validity_mask`
28	- `segment_sum` and `segment_mean`
29	- `edge_force_virial`
30	
31	The file layout is your choice; hidden verification checks these public
32	behaviors through the package namespace rather than requiring a particular
33	internal module split.
34	
35	The derivative contract is also part of the public behavior. For
36	`edge_vec = r_src - r_dst` and `g = dE / d(edge_vec)`, use
37	
38	```text
39	F_k = sum(g for edges with dst=k) - sum(g for edges with src=k)
40	edge_virial = -outer(g, edge_vec)
41	```
42	
43	Attribute a complete edge virial to its source atom, ignore masked guard edges,
44	and return one `(3, 3)` virial per frame. Reject non-positive cutoffs and
45	inconsistent coordinate, type, or cell shapes with `ValueError` rather than
46	silently producing an empty or misaligned graph.
47	
48	The result must be a coherent workflow, not a fixture-specific patch. It must
49	support more than the public coordinates, more than one frame, and more than
50	one edge count. Do not hard-code atom indices, distances, edge counts, force
51	values, or a particular periodic cell. Keep the sign and tensor-layout
52	conventions explicit in code and documentation so a downstream model can rely
53	on them.
54	
55	The public reproduction is only a starting point. A successful solution must
56	also preserve ordinary non-periodic behavior while adding the missing general
57	scientific cases.

# Scientific method context
## 1. Why a local edge graph is part of the model, not just a data structure
Deep-potential atomistic models describe an energy from local environments. The
environment of a center atom is formed from neighboring atoms and their
relative displacement vectors. The model therefore needs a consistent answer to
three questions: which atoms are neighbors, what displacement vector represents
each pair, and how periodic images map back to the local atoms whose forces must
be reported.
The DeePMD literature emphasizes local frames, symmetry-preserving descriptors,
and differentiable energy-to-force evaluation. A graph representation makes
these contracts explicit: an edge has a source atom, a destination/center atom,
and a vector such as `r_src - r_dst`. The edge list is not an arbitrary graph;
it is a geometric representation of a physical interaction neighborhood.
## 2. Periodic boundary conditions
For a periodic simulation cell, an atom may be a neighbor only through an image
of the cell. The minimum-image displacement, or an equivalent explicit ghost
image, must be used. A pair that is far apart in the displayed cell can still
be within the cutoff after a lattice translation. The image contribution must
be accumulated onto the local owner of that atom rather than reported as a new
physical atom.
Non-periodic systems have no such images. The implementation must keep these
two geometries distinct and must not manufacture periodic neighbors when no
cell is supplied.
## 3. Padding and masks
Compiled backends often need a fixed maximum edge axis. Padding edges are shape
guards, not physical interactions. They must be represented by an explicit mask
and must contribute zero to every downstream reduction. Real edges should form
a compact prefix, with masked guard edges after them. A similar compact-prefix
principle applies to a padded node axis: per-frame node counts define which
nodes are real.
## 4. From edge derivatives to observables
Let `e = r_src - r_dst` and let `g = dE/de`. With the convention used by the
source development, the force on a node is the signed scatter
```text
F_k = sum(g for edges with dst=k) - sum(g for edges with src=k)
```
An edge virial contribution is the outer product `-g outer e`. The source
development attributes the full edge contribution to the source atom for the
per-atom virial, while the global virial remains a sum over physical edges.
For multiple frames, the global virial is one `(3, 3)` tensor per frame, not a
single tensor that silently collapses frames. Empty frames must produce a zero
tensor.
## 5. Reading guide
The main software reference is the DeePMD-kit package and its cited papers:
- DeePMD-kit v2: <https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0155600>
- Original deep potential method: <https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.143001>
- DeePMD-kit repository: <https://github.com/deepmodeling/deepmd-kit>
- The upstream NeighborGraph change and its tests are linked in the task
author's provenance notes, but are intentionally not copied into the public
task payload.
The goal is not to reproduce a neural-network checkpoint. It is to reconstruct
the geometry and differential-observable contract that a backend-agnostic
atomistic model consumes.

"""Masks and segment reductions over the flat axes of a NeighborGraph.

Axis conventions
----------------
The node axis of a :class:`~deepmd.dpmodel.utils.neighbor_graph.NeighborGraph`
is flat with length ``N = sum(n_node)``; frame ``f`` owns the contiguous slice
``offsets[f] : offsets[f] + n_node[f]`` with ``offsets`` the exclusive prefix
sum of ``n_node``. When the node axis is padded to a static ``node_capacity``,
the real nodes always form the prefix ``: sum(n_node)`` — empty frames own an
empty slice — and the remaining tail is padding.

Segment reductions scatter rows of ``data`` onto integer segment ids; empty
segments reduce to zero (never NaN).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from deepmd.dpmodel.array_api import xp_add_at, xp_asarray, xp_zeros


def _as_node_counts(n_node) -> np.ndarray:
    counts = np.asarray(n_node, dtype=np.int64)
    if counts.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"n_node must be a 1-D per-frame count array, got shape {counts.shape}")
    if counts.size and counts.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError("n_node must be non-negative")
    return counts


def frame_offsets(n_node) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the exclusive prefix sum of ``n_node``: flat start index per frame."""
    counts = _as_node_counts(n_node)
    return np.cumsum(counts) - counts


def frame_of_node(n_node) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the (N,) frame id of every real node on the flat node axis."""
    counts = _as_node_counts(n_node)
    return np.repeat(np.arange(counts.size, dtype=np.int64), counts)


def node_validity_mask(n_node, node_capacity=None):
    """Boolean node mask for a padded flat node axis.
    ...

    counts = _as_node_counts(n_node)
    total = int(counts.sum())
    capacity = total if node_capacity is None else int(node_capacity)
    if capacity < total:
        raise ValueError(...)
    mask = np.zeros(capacity, dtype=bool)
    mask[:total] = True
    return mask

"""Validity masks and segment reductions over flat graph axes.

Axis conventions shared by the whole neighbor-graph capability:

* The node axis of a
  :class:`~deepmd.dpmodel.utils.neighbor_graph.NeighborGraph` is flat with
  length ``N = sum(n_node)``; frame ``f`` owns the contiguous slice
  ``offsets[f] : offsets[f] + n_node[f]`` where ``offsets`` is the exclusive
  prefix sum of ``n_node``. An empty frame owns an empty slice.
* When the node axis is padded to a static ``node_capacity``, the real nodes
  form the prefix ``: sum(n_node)`` and the tail is padding. The same
  compact-prefix rule holds for the edge axis: real edges first, masked guard
  edges after.
* Segment reductions scatter rows of ``data`` onto integer segment ids; empty
  segments reduce to zero, never NaN.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from deepmd.dpmodel.array_api import xp_add_at, xp_asarray, xp_zeros


def as_node_counts(n_node) -> np.ndarray:
    """Validate ``n_node`` as a 1-D array of non-negative per-frame counts."""
    counts = np.asarray(n_node, dtype=np.int64)
    if counts.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"n_node must be a 1-D per-frame count array, got shape {counts.shape}"
        )
    if counts.size and counts.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError("n_node entries must be non-negative")
    return counts


def frame_offsets(n_node) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the flat start index of each frame: the exclusive prefix sum
    of ``n_node``. Frame ``f`` owns ``offsets[f] : offsets[f] + n_node[f]``."""
    counts = as_node_counts(n_node)
    return np.cumsum(counts) - counts


def frame_of_node(n_node) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the ``(N,)`` frame id of every real node on the flat node axis."""
    counts = as_node_counts(n_node)
    return np.repeat(np.arange(counts.size, dtype=np.int64), counts)


def node_validity_mask(n_node, node_capacity=None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Boolean mask selecting the real nodes of a padded flat node axis.

    Real nodes always form the prefix ``: sum(n_node)`` because frames are
    packed contiguously and empty frames own empty slices; the tail up to
    ``node_capacity`` is padding.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_node : (n_frame,) int
        Real node count per frame.
    node_capacity : int, optional
        Static node-axis length. Defaults to ``sum(n_node)`` (no padding).

    Returns
    -------
    (node_capacity,) bool
        ``True`` for real nodes, ``False`` for padding.
    """
    counts = as_node_counts(n_node)
    total = int(counts.sum())
    capacity = total if node_capacity is None else int(node_capacity)
    if capacity < total:
        raise ValueError(
            f"node_capacity {capacity} is smaller than the real node count {total}"
        )
    mask = xp_zeros((capacity,), dtype=bool)
    mask[:total] = True
    return mask


def _validate_segment_args(data, segment_ids, num_segments):
    arr = xp_asarray(data)
    if arr.ndim == 0:
        raise ValueError("data must have at least one row axis")
    ids = np.asarray(segment_ids, dtype=np.int64)
    if ids.ndim != 1 or ids.shape[0] != arr.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"segment_ids must be a 1-D array with one id per data row, got "
            f"data shape {arr.shape} and segment_ids shape {ids.shape}"
        )
    n_seg = int(num_segments)
    if n_seg < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"num_segments must be non-negative, got {n_seg}")
    if ids.size and (ids.min() < 0 or ids.max() >= n_seg):
        raise ValueError(
            f"segment_ids must lie in [0, {n_seg}), got "
            f"[{ids.min()}, {ids.max()}]"
        )
    return arr, ids, n_seg


def segment_sum(data, segment_ids, num_segments) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sum rows of ``data`` per segment id.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : (N, ...)
        Rows to scatter onto segments.
    segment_ids : (N,) int
        Segment id of each row, in ``[0, num_segments)``.
    num_segments : int
        Number of output segments; segments with no rows are zero.

    Returns
    -------
    (num_segments, ...)
        ``out[s]`` is the sum of all rows whose id is ``s``.
    """
    arr, ids, n_seg = _validate_segment_args(data, segment_ids, num_segments)
    out = xp_zeros((n_seg,) + arr.shape[1:], dtype=arr.dtype)
    if ids.size:
        xp_add_at(out, ids, arr)
    return out


def segment_mean(data, segment_ids, num_segments) -> np.ndarray:
    """Average rows of ``data`` per segment id.

    Same contract as :func:`segment_sum`, except each segment sum is divided
    by its row count. Empty segments are zero (no division by zero), which
    keeps padded and empty-frame reductions finite.
    """
    arr, ids, n_seg = _validate_segment_args(data, segment_ids, num_segments)
    dtype = np.result_type(arr.dtype, np.float64)
    sums = xp_zeros((n_seg,) + arr.shape[1:], dtype=dtype)
    if ids.size:
        xp_add_at(sums, ids, arr.astype(dtype, copy=False))
    counts = np.bincount(ids, minlength=n_seg).astype(dtype)
    denom = np.maximum(counts, 1.0).reshape((n_seg,) + (1,) * (sums.ndim - 1))
    return sums / denom

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later
"""Geometry to :class:`NeighborGraph` conversion.

Scientific conventions
----------------------
* Every graph node is a *local*, real atom: virtual atoms (``atype < 0``) are
  dropped from the node axis, and a frame with no real atoms simply gets
  ``n_node[f] == 0`` (an empty frame — a valid scientific situation).
* An edge is a directed ordered pair ``src -> dst``: ``dst`` is the center
  atom whose local environment the edge belongs to, ``src`` is the neighbor,
  and ``edge_vec = r_src - r_dst`` is the displacement used by the energy
  model. Both directions of a pair appear when both atoms are within each
  other's cutoff.
* The cutoff is inclusive: pairs with ``0 < |edge_vec| <= rcut`` are edges.
  The identical-image self pair (distance 0) is never an edge.
* Periodic systems are expanded into ghost images. Along each cell axis the
  images span ``ceil(rcut / face_distance)`` lattice shifts, so *every* image
  within the cutoff yields an edge — including multiple images of the same
  pair and an atom's own non-home images when the cell is smaller than the
  cutoff. Image semantics live entirely in ``edge_vec``: the edge's ``src``
  stays the local owner of the image, which is what lets force and virial
  accumulation land on physical atoms.
* Edges are deterministic and compact: frame by frame, grouped by destination
  atom; within one destination, ordered by increasing distance, then neighbor
  index, then lattice shift. Real edges form a prefix of the edge axis; the
  tail is filled with masked guard edges (``edge_mask == False``, zero
  ``edge_vec``, zero indices) sized by :class:`GraphLayout`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools

import numpy as np

from .graph_ops import frame_offsets
from .neighbor_graph import GraphLayout, NeighborGraph
from .region import normalize_coord, to_face_distance


def _as_frame_array(coord, atype):
    """Validate coordinates and types as aligned ``(n_frame, n_atom, ...)``
    arrays, accepting the legacy flat ``(n_frame, 3 * n_atom)`` coordinate
    layout."""
    xyz = np.asarray(coord, dtype=np.float64)
    if xyz.ndim == 2 and xyz.shape[1] % 3 == 0:
        xyz = xyz.reshape(xyz.shape[0], -1, 3)
    if xyz.ndim != 3 or xyz.shape[2] != 3:
        raise ValueError(
            "coord must have shape (n_frame, n_atom, 3) or (n_frame, 3*n_atom), "
            f"got {xyz.shape}"
        )
    types = np.asarray(atype, dtype=np.int64)
    if types.shape != xyz.shape[:2]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"atype shape {types.shape} does not match the coordinate frames "
            f"{xyz.shape[:2]}"
        )
    return xyz, types


def _as_cells(cell, n_frame):
    """Validate the optional periodic cell as one ``(3, 3)`` cell per frame.

    A single ``(3, 3)`` cell broadcasts to all frames; ``(n_frame, 9)`` is the
    legacy flat layout. Singular cells cannot define periodic images and are
    rejected."""
    if cell is None:
        return None
    arr = np.asarray(cell, dtype=np.float64)
    if arr.ndim == 3 and arr.shape == (n_frame, 3, 3):
        cells = arr
    elif arr.ndim == 2 and arr.shape == (n_frame, 9):
        cells = arr.reshape(n_frame, 3, 3)
    elif arr.shape == (3, 3):
        cells = np.broadcast_to(arr, (n_frame, 3, 3))
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"cell must be None, (3, 3), (n_frame, 3, 3), or (n_frame, 9) with "
            f"n_frame={n_frame}, got shape {arr.shape}"
        )
    cells = np.array(cells, dtype=np.float64, copy=True)
    if not np.isfinite(cells).all():
        raise ValueError("cell must contain only finite values")
    if np.any(np.abs(np.linalg.det(cells)) <= 1e-12):
        raise ValueError("cell must be non-singular in every frame")
    return cells


def _as_cutoff(rcut):
    """Validate the neighbor cutoff as a positive scalar."""
    try:
        value = float(rcut)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError(f"cutoff must be a positive scalar, got {rcut!r}") from None
    if not np.isfinite(value) or value <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"cutoff must be a positive finite scalar, got {value}")
    return value


def _frame_edges(xyz, cell, rcut):
    """Ordered neighbor edges of one frame of real atoms.

    Parameters
    ----------
    xyz : (n, 3) float
        Real-atom coordinates, wrapped into ``cell`` when periodic.
    cell : (3, 3) float or None
        Periodic cell; ``None`` means an ordinary non-periodic frame (a
        single zero lattice shift — no images are manufactured).
    rcut : float
        Inclusive cutoff.

    Returns
    -------
    src, dst, vec : (E,) int, (E,) int, (E, 3) float
        Edges sorted by (dst, distance, src, shift) with
        ``vec = r_src_image - r_dst``.
    """
    n_atom = xyz.shape[0]
    empty = (
        np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64),
        np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64),
        np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float64),
    )
    if n_atom == 0:
        return empty
    if cell is None:
        # One zero shift: identical geometry, no periodic images.
        shifts = np.zeros((1, 3), dtype=np.float64)
        images = xyz[None, :, :]
    else:
        face = np.maximum(to_face_distance(cell), 1e-12)
        bound = np.ceil(float(rcut) / face).astype(np.int64)
        shifts = sorted(
            itertools.product(*(range(-int(b), int(b) + 1) for b in bound)),
            key=lambda shift: (sum(v * v for v in shift), shift),
        )
        shifts = np.asarray(shifts, dtype=np.float64)
        images = xyz[None, :, :] + shifts[:, None, :] @ cell
    flat = images.reshape(-1, 3)  # shift-major: index = shift * n_atom + atom
    part_src, part_dst, part_vec = [], [], []
    part_dist, part_shift = [], []
    for center in range(n_atom):
        diff = flat - xyz[center]
        dist = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.einsum("ij,ij->i", diff, diff), 0.0))
        keep = np.flatnonzero((dist > 0.0) & (dist <= rcut))
        part_dst.append(np.full(keep.size, center, dtype=np.int64))
        part_src.append((keep % n_atom).astype(np.int64))
        part_shift.append((keep // n_atom).astype(np.int64))
        part_dist.append(dist[keep])
        part_vec.append(diff[keep])
    if not any(part.size for part in part_dst):
        return empty
    dst = np.concatenate(part_dst)
    src = np.concatenate(part_src)
    shift = np.concatenate(part_shift)
    dist = np.concatenate(part_dist)
    vec = np.concatenate(part_vec, axis=0)
    order = np.lexsort((shift, src, dist, dst))
    return src[order], dst[order], vec[order]


def _apply_frame_capacity(n_node, layout):
    """Pad the frame axis with empty frames up to ``layout.frame_capacity``."""
    capacity = getattr(layout, "frame_capacity", None) if layout is not None else None
    if capacity is None:
        return n_node
    capacity = int(capacity)
    if capacity < n_node.size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"frame_capacity {capacity} is smaller than the frame count {n_node.size}"
        )
    padded = np.zeros(capacity, dtype=np.int64)
    padded[: n_node.size] = n_node
    return padded


def _assemble_graph(n_node, per_frame_edges, layout):
    """Pack per-frame edges into one padded :class:`NeighborGraph`.

    Node indices of frame ``f`` are shifted by the frame's flat offset; real
    edges form a compact prefix and masked guard edges fill the tail. The edge
    axis length follows the layout policy: ``edge_capacity`` when the layout
    pins a static shape, otherwise ``max(n_real_edges, min_edges)`` for a
    dynamic but non-degenerate axis.

    offsets = frame_offsets(n_node)

        all_dst = np.concatenate(dst_parts)
        all_vec = np.concatenate(vec_parts, axis=0)
    else:
        all_src = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
        all_dst = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64)
        all_vec = np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    edge_capacity = getattr(layout, "edge_capacity", None) if layout is not None else None
    min_edges = int(getattr(layout, "min_edges", 2)) if layout is not None else 2
    if edge_capacity is not None:
        target = int(edge_capacity)
        if target < n_real:
            raise ValueError(
                f"edge_capacity {target} is smaller than the real edge count "
                f"{n_real}; grow the capacity instead of dropping edges"
            )
    else:
        target = max(n_real, min_edges)
    edge_index = np.zeros((2, target), dtype=np.int64)
    edge_vec = np.zeros((target, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    edge_mask = np.zeros(target, dtype=bool)
    if n_real:
        edge_index[0, :n_real] = all_src
        edge_index[1, :n_real] = all_dst

        n_node=n_node,
        edge_index=edge_index,
        edge_vec=edge_vec,
        edge_mask=edge_mask,
        # Every node on the flat axis is a local atom; images enter only
        # through edge vectors, never as nodes.
        n_local=n_node.copy(),
    )


def build_neighbor_graph(coord, atype, cell=None, rcut=None, layout=None):
    """Build a :class:`NeighborGraph` from coordinates, types and an optional
    periodic cell.

    Parameters
    ----------
    coord : (n_frame, n_atom, 3) or (n_frame, 3*n_atom) float
        Atom coordinates. Frames may be empty or hold virtual atoms.
    atype : (n_frame, n_atom) int
        Atom types; negative types mark virtual atoms, which are dropped from
        the node axis.
    cell : None, (3, 3), (n_frame, 3, 3) or (n_frame, 9) float
        Periodic cell. ``None`` selects the ordinary non-periodic path and no
        image edges are manufactured.
    rcut : float
        Positive neighbor cutoff; pairs with ``0 < distance <= rcut`` become
        edges.
    layout : GraphLayout, optional
        Static-length policy for the padded edge/frame axes. Real edges are
        never dropped: an ``edge_capacity`` below the real edge count raises
        ``ValueError``.

    -------
    NeighborGraph
        Flat graph with ``edge_vec = r_src - r_dst`` for every real edge and
        masked, zero-valued guard edges padding the tail.
    """

    xyz, types = _as_frame_array(coord, atype)
    cells = _as_cells(cell, xyz.shape[0])
    n_frame = types.shape[0]

    per_frame_edges = []
    for frame in range(n_frame):
        real = types[frame] >= 0
        frame_xyz = xyz[frame][real]
        if cells is not None and frame_xyz.shape[0]:
            frame_xyz = normalize_coord(frame_xyz, cells[frame])

            _frame_edges(
                frame_xyz,
                None if cells is None else cells[frame],
                cutoff,
            )
        )
    n_node = _apply_frame_capacity(n_node, layout)

def from_dense_quartet(extended_coord, nlist, mapping, layout=None):
    """Adapt the legacy dense representation to a :class:`NeighborGraph`.

    The legacy path materializes periodic images explicitly: ``extended_coord``
    holds local atoms followed by ghost images, the dense neighbor list
    ``nlist`` stores extended indices (``-1`` padding) per local center, and
    ``mapping`` folds every extended atom back to its local owner. One edge is
    emitted per non-negative ``nlist`` entry, in (center, slot) order:

    * ``dst = center`` (a local atom),
    * ``src = mapping[j]`` — the *owner* of neighbor entry ``j``, so a ghost
      image contributes to its physical local atom,
    * ``edge_vec = extended_coord[j] - extended_coord[center]``, which keeps
      the periodic-image displacement semantics of the dense path.

    The node axis contains only local atoms, so ``n_node[f] == nlist.shape[1]``
    per frame.

    Parameters
    ----------
    extended_coord : (n_frame, n_all, 3) or (n_frame, 3*n_all) float
        Local atoms followed by their periodic images.
    nlist : (n_frame, n_local, n_sel) int
        Dense neighbor indices into the extended axis; negative is padding.
    mapping : (n_frame, n_all) int
        Owner local index of each extended atom; negative marks unusable
        padding rows, whose neighbor entries are skipped.
    layout : GraphLayout, optional
        Static-length policy, same contract as :func:`build_neighbor_graph`.

    Returns
    -------
    NeighborGraph
    """
    xyz = np.asarray(extended_coord, dtype=np.float64)
    if xyz.ndim == 2 and xyz.shape[1] % 3 == 0:
        xyz = xyz.reshape(xyz.shape[0], -1, 3)
    if xyz.ndim != 3 or xyz.shape[2] != 3:
        raise ValueError(
            "extended_coord must have shape (n_frame, n_all, 3) or "
            f"(n_frame, 3*n_all), got {xyz.shape}"
        )
    n_frame, n_all = xyz.shape[:2]
    nlist = np.asarray(nlist, dtype=np.int64)
    if nlist.ndim != 3 or nlist.shape[0] != n_frame:
        raise ValueError(
            f"nlist must have shape (n_frame, n_local, n_sel) with "
            f"n_frame={n_frame}, got {nlist.shape}"
        )
    n_local = nlist.shape[1]
    if n_local > n_all:
        raise ValueError(
            f"dense nlist has {n_local} centers but the extended axis holds "
            f"only {n_all} atoms"
        )
    mapping = np.asarray(mapping, dtype=np.int64)
    if mapping.shape != (n_frame, n_all):
        raise ValueError(
            f"mapping must have shape {(n_frame, n_all)}, got {mapping.shape}"
        )
    per_frame_edges = []
    for frame in range(n_frame):
        part_src, part_dst, part_vec = [], [], []
        for center in range(n_local):
            for entry in nlist[frame, center]:
                j = int(entry)
                if j < 0:
                    continue
                if j >= n_all:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"neighbor index {j} is out of range for {n_all} "
                        "extended atoms"
                    )
                owner = int(mapping[frame, j])
                if owner < 0:
                    continue
                if owner >= n_local:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"owner index {owner} is out of range for {n_local} "
                        "local atoms"
                    )
                part_src.append(owner)
                part_dst.append(center)
                part_vec.append(xyz[frame, j] - xyz[frame, center])
        if part_dst:
            per_frame_edges.append(
                (
                    np.asarray(part_src, dtype=np.int64),
                    np.asarray(part_dst, dtype=np.int64),
                    np.asarray(part_vec, dtype=np.float64),
                )
            )
        else:
            per_frame_edges.append(
                (
                    np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64),
                    np.zeros(0, dtype=np.int64),
                    np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=np.float64),
                )
            )
    n_node = np.full(n_frame, n_local, dtype=np.int64)
    n_node = _apply_frame_capacity(n_node, layout)
    return _assemble_graph(n_node, per_frame_edges, layout)

# SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later
"""Energy-derivative to force / virial assembly on a :class:`NeighborGraph`.

Sign and tensor-layout conventions (public contract)
----------------------------------------------------
Every edge stores ``edge_vec = r_src - r_dst`` with ``dst`` the center atom
and ``src`` the neighbor. Given per-edge energy derivatives
``g = dE / d(edge_vec)`` of shape ``(E, 3)``:

* Force on node ``k``::

      F_k = sum(g  for edges with dst == k) - sum(g  for edges with src == k)

  This is the physical force: the negative gradient of the total edge energy
  with respect to the node position, because ``d(edge_vec)/d(r_dst) = -I``
  and ``d(edge_vec)/d(r_src) = +I``.

* Edge virial::

      virial_e = -outer(g_e, edge_vec_e)        # (3, 3), row = derivative axis

  The *complete* edge virial is attributed to the source atom of the edge for
  the per-atom virial; empty and padded nodes hold zero.

* Frame virial: one ``(3, 3)`` tensor per frame, the sum of ``virial_e`` over
  the real edges of the frame (an edge belongs to the frame of its
  destination/center node). Frames without edges give a zero tensor — the
  per-frame axis is never collapsed.

Guard edges (``edge_mask == False``) contribute exactly zero to every output,
regardless of what their (zero-filled) slots contain.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

from deepmd.dpmodel.array_api import xp_add_at, xp_zeros

from .graph_ops import as_node_counts, frame_of_node


def edge_force_virial(gradients, edge_vec, edge_index, edge_mask, n_node,
                      node_capacity=None):
    """Assemble per-atom forces, per-atom virials and per-frame virials.

    Parameters
    ----------
    gradients : (E, 3) float
        Edge derivatives ``g = dE / d(edge_vec)``.
    edge_vec : (E, 3) float
        Edge displacements ``r_src - r_dst``.
    edge_index : (2, E) int
        ``[src, dst]`` node indices; ``src`` = neighbor, ``dst`` = center.
    edge_mask : (E,) bool
        ``True`` for real edges, ``False`` for padded guard edges, which are
        ignored entirely.
    n_node : (n_frame,) int
        Real node count per frame on the flat node axis.
    node_capacity : int, optional
        Static node-axis length; must cover ``sum(n_node)``. Defaults to
        ``sum(n_node)`` (no padding). Padded nodes return zero rows.

    Returns
    -------
    force : (node_capacity, 3) float
        ``F_k = sum_{dst=k} g - sum_{src=k} g``.
    atom_virial : (node_capacity, 3, 3) float
        ``sum_{src=k} -outer(g, edge_vec)`` — the complete edge virial is
        attributed to the source atom.
    virial : (n_frame, 3, 3) float
        One virial per frame, summing ``-outer(g, edge_vec)`` over the real
        edges of each frame.
    """
    vec = np.asarray(edge_vec, dtype=np.float64)
    if vec.ndim != 2 or vec.shape[1] != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"edge_vec must have shape (n_edge, 3), got {vec.shape}")
    n_edge = vec.shape[0]
    grad = np.asarray(gradients, dtype=np.float64)
    if grad.shape != vec.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"gradients shape {grad.shape} must match edge_vec shape {vec.shape}"
        )
    index = np.asarray(edge_index, dtype=np.int64)
    if index.shape != (2, n_edge):
        raise ValueError(
            f"edge_index must have shape (2, {n_edge}), got {index.shape}"
        )
    mask = np.asarray(edge_mask, dtype=bool)
    if mask.shape != (n_edge,):
        raise ValueError(
            f"edge_mask must have shape ({n_edge},), got {mask.shape}"
        )
    counts = as_node_counts(n_node)
    n_real_nodes = int(counts.sum())
    if node_capacity is None:
        capacity = n_real_nodes
    else:
        capacity = int(node_capacity)
        if capacity < n_real_nodes:
            raise ValueError(
                f"node_capacity {capacity} is smaller than the real node count "
                f"{n_real_nodes}"
            )
    src = index[0][mask]
    dst = index[1][mask]
    if src.size:
        low = int(min(src.min(), dst.min()))
        high = int(max(src.max(), dst.max()))
        if low < 0 or high >= n_real_nodes:
            raise ValueError(
                f"real edges must reference real nodes in [0, {n_real_nodes}), "
                f"got range [{low}, {high}]"
            )
    grad_real = grad[mask]
    vec_real = vec[mask]
    # F_k = sum(g | dst=k) - sum(g | src=k)
    force = xp_zeros((capacity, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    xp_add_at(force, dst, grad_real)
    xp_add_at(force, src, -grad_real)
    # edge_virial = -outer(g, edge_vec); complete attribution to the source.
    edge_virial = -np.einsum("ei,ej->eij", grad_real, vec_real)
    atom_virial = xp_zeros((capacity, 3, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    xp_add_at(atom_virial, src, edge_virial)
    # One (3, 3) virial per frame: scatter by the destination node's frame.
    edge_frame = frame_of_node(counts)[dst]
    virial = xp_zeros((counts.size, 3, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    xp_add_at(virial, edge_frame, edge_virial)
    return force, atom_virial, virial

## What was added

**`source/deepmd/dpmodel/utils/graph_build.py`** — the two geometry builders:
- `build_neighbor_graph(coord, atype, cell=None, rcut=None, layout=None)` handles ordinary and periodic systems with one code path: non-periodic frames get a single zero lattice shift, while periodic frames are expanded into ghost images spanning `ceil(rcut/face_distance)` shifts per axis — so multiple images of one pair and an atom's own periodic images are all real edges when within the inclusive cutoff `0 < |v| <= rcut`. Inputs are wrapped into the cell first, so out-of-cell coordinates and per-frame skewed cells work. Virtual atoms (`atype < 0`) are dropped and nodes reindexed; empty frames get `n_node=0`; isolated atoms stay as edge-less nodes.
- `from_dense_quartet(extended_coord, nlist, mapping, layout=None)` adapts the legacy dense representation: `dst = center`, `src = mapping[j]` folds each ghost neighbor to its local owner, and `edge_vec` keeps the ghost displacement, preserving periodic-image semantics.

Guard edges contribute exactly zero; out-of-range real indices raise `ValueError`.
